To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gating of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors (IP3Rs), the Ca(2+) channels of the endoplasmatic reticulum, is coupled, and that this coupling is important for the termination of Ca(2+ )puffs.

the termination of Ca(2+)(i) signals mediated by Ca2+ release through clusters of ino-sitol trisphophate receptors (IP3Rs) depends on Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release, which is terminated in part by the coupling of IP3R gating.

the kinetics of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor channel closing during termination of calcium puffs in intact cells is nonrandom and that this behavior cannot readily be attributed to Ca2+-inactivation or local ER Ca2+ depletion.

the mechanisms of Ca(2+), IP3 and CaMK II regulation of the IP3R channel, and the mechanisms of calcium puffs, Ca(2+) oscillations and waves in the cell.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gating of IP3R clusters is coupled, possibly through allosteric interactions.
the gating kinetics of individual IP3Rs during puffs are consistent with a mechanism in which IP3Rs can be closed by Ca(2+), but the closing of one channel is coupled with that of its neighbors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca(2+) signaling in the cell is a complex process that is not only controlled by the concentration of Ca(2+), but by the number of Ca(2) channels that are open and how they are coupled.
we found that the gating of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor channel (IP3R channel) clusters in the endoplasmatic reticulum is coupled.
the termination of puffs and the closing of IP3R clusters is not a random, stochastic process, but rather is controlled by a coordinated mechanism that ensures that all channels close together.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca(2+) puffs are terminated by coordinated closing of IP3R clusters, which may be a common termination mechanism for localized Ca(2+), and other signals, that are mediated by channel clustering.
the gating of IP3R Ca2+ channels is highly cooperative, and this may be a general feature of other ER channels as well.
Ca(2+), which is the trigger of Ca(2+)(i) puffs, also terminates the Ca(2+)-(i) signal by closing the IP3Rs.
